question: Does a timeout before a late free throw make the shooter miss?
answer: Icing doesn't work. Iced shooters were +2.3 points better than un-iced shooters, relative to their own FT% (CI +0.0 to +4.6).
findings: Iced shooters made 71.2% (CI 68.9-73.4), against their usual 72.5%, n=1567.
Shooters who weren't iced made 69.9% (CI 69.5-70.2), against their usual 73.4%, n=59853.
Iced minus not iced, against their own FT%, is +2.3 points (95% CI +0.0 to +4.6).
method: The sample is the first FT of a trip in the last 2:00 of regulation or OT, with the margin within 3. A shooter is iced when the defense calls timeout between the foul and the FT. The outcome is made minus the shooter's leave-one-out FT% (min 20 other FTs), with a game-clustered bootstrap.
data: ESPN play-by-play via sportsdataverse, CBB, 2011-12 to 2025-26, 61,420 first free throws.
split_check: Iced minus not iced was +2.0 points in 2012-19 (CI -1.0 to +4.8) and +2.5 in 2020-26 (CI -0.8 to +6.1).
